summary: Packed into just 1.4 square miles in the eastern Coachella Valley, Hillcrest squeezes over 10,000 residents into a density rivaling mid-size urban cores — yet it sits in a landscape of open desert sky, date palm groves, and the stark wall of the Little San Bernardino Mountains to the north. That juxtaposition defines daily life: average daytime highs around 80°F year-round and nearly ten hours of sunshine per day mean summer heat is a serious planning factor, with July and August routinely pushing well past 110°F. The median home value of roughly $250,000 against a median household income near $45,000 yields a price-to-income ratio around 5.6 — stretched but not impossible for buyers, while median rent at about $1,197 consumes roughly 32% of that same income. The local economy leans heavily on agriculture, logistics, and service-sector work tied to the broader Coachella Valley corridor, making this functionally a place where many commute west toward Palm Desert or Indio for employment. A poverty rate near 29% and school math proficiency scores averaging more than 100 points below standard signal real structural challenges alongside that affordable-for-Southern-California price tag. Hillcrest is a place where desert affordability and desert hardship arrive in the same package.
